elements.char: Abstract
elements.label: text

elements.char: Proteins in cellular environments are highly susceptible. Local perturbations to any residue
elements.label: text

elements.char: can be sensed by other spatially distal residues in the protein molecule, showing long-range
elements.label: text

elements.char: correlations in the native dynamics of proteins. The long-range correlations of proteins
elements.label: text

elements.char: contribute to many biological processes such as allostery, catalysis, and transportation.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Revealing the structural origin of such long-range correlations is of great significance in
elements.label: text

elements.char: understanding the design principle of biologically functional proteins. In this work, based on
elements.label: text

elements.char: a large set of globular proteins determined by X-ray crystallography, by conducting normal
elements.label: text

elements.char: mode analysis with the elastic network models, we demonstrate that such long-range corre-
elements.label: text

elements.char: lations are encoded in the native topology of the proteins. To understand how native topol-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ogy defines the structure and the dynamics of the proteins, we conduct scaling analysis on
elements.label: text

elements.char: the size dependence of the slowest vibration mode, average path length, and modularity.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Our results quantitatively describe how native proteins balance between order and disorder,
elements.label: text

elements.char: showing both dense packing and fractal topology. It is suggested that the balance between
elements.label: text

elements.char: stability and flexibility acts as an evolutionary constraint for proteins at different sizes. Over-
elements.label: text

elements.char: all, our result not only gives a new perspective bridging the protein structure and its dynam-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ics but also reveals a universal principle in the evolution of proteins at all different sizes.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Author summary
elements.label: text

elements.char: The long-range correlated fluctuations are closely related to many biological processes of
elements.label: text

elements.char: the proteins, such as catalysis, ligand binding, biomolecular recognition, and transporta-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tion. In this paper, we elucidate the structural origin of the long-range correlation and
elements.label: text

elements.char: describe how native contact topology defines the slow-mode dynamics of the native pro-
elements.label: text

elements.char: teins. Our result suggests an evolutionary constraint for proteins at different sizes, which
elements.label: text

elements.char: may shed light on solving many biophysical problems such as structure prediction, multi-
elements.label: text

elements.char: scale molecular simulations, and the design of molecular machines. Moreover, in statisti-
elements.label: text

elements.char: cal physics, as the long-range correlations are notable signs of the critical point, unveiling
elements.label: text

elements.char: the origin of such criticality can extend our understanding of the organizing principle of a
elements.label: text

elements.char: large variety of complex systems.
